A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SpatialLLM study, including complete figures, tables and Appendices A–C. Pages 2–14 have identical extracted text and rendered images; first-page differences concern author information and the version stamp.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original SpatialVQA evaluations, including model comparisons in Table 1 and architecture, data and training ablations in Table 2.

after.justification: The same original SpatialVQA experiments, comparative results and ablations remain in Section 4 and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix A retain identical model components, data-generation procedures, mixed visual encoders, 3D-informed alignment and instruction-tuning methods.

E1.justification: Both retain the same ImageNet3D/OpenImages-derived and standard training datasets, plus SpatialVQA evaluation covering urban and indoor scenes and distance, orientation and spatial-relation questions.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same seven comparators, including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and SpatialVLM-13B. Table 2 also retains the same design variants; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.1, Table 2 and Appendix B retain identical training configurations, accuracy metrics and the 1,323-question SpatialVQA evaluation set. No experimental setting or evaluation procedure changes.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same encoder, language-model, alignment-data, instruction-tuning and encoder-pretraining ablations. The roadmap analysis and qualitative comparisons in Figures 6–7 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point accuracies without seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical. For example, Table 1 retains average accuracies of 62.7% for SpatialLLM, 54.0% for GPT-4o and 52.2% for SpatialVLM-13B.

T1.justification: The task definitions and reasoning descriptions are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about SpatialVQA, orientation-aware training data, the compound design and SpatialLLM's comparative performance.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same explanations of data-quality benefits and possible generalizability loss from encoder pretraining. The comparison scope and rationale for excluding SpatialRGPT also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The LLaVA-v1.5-based hyperparameter guidance, eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs and Appendix A data-generation details are unchanged. Appendix C still promises future code and data releases without adding access information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning relative to SpatialVLM and SpatialRGPT, and all 70 reference entries are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first page places Jieneng Chen before Alan Yuille instead of after him and changes 'Correspondence to' to 'Corresponding author:'. The scientific prose and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: First-page typesetting changes slightly: an envelope replaces the correspondence asterisk, the author line is reset, and the version/date stamp shifts position. Figures 1–8, Tables 1–2 and subsequent page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision changes only first-page author information and presentation. The scientific content, supporting evidence, explanations and reproducibility information—including Appendices A–C—remain identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
